what: 14-agent why-no-edge audit: 7 analysis dimensions (signal-vs-random, filter-attribution, exit-leak, cost-drag, beta-regime, statistics-selection, breakout-premise), each adversarially re-derived by an independent verifier. Synthesis in docs/WHY_NO_EDGE.md; scripts in backtest/audit/.

analysis.headline: The entry rule has a small, short-lived (+4h) timing effect but adds no system-level expectancy over regime-matched random timing on any symbol: vs 200 seeded random-entry engine runs the real net returns sit at the 91.0th (EURUSD), 84.5th (GBPUSD), 44.0th (USDJPY) and 29.5th (XAUUSD) percentiles — none clears 95, and XAUUSD's +1.73% is below the random median of +3.60%.

analysis.conclusion: Verdict for the WHY-no-edge synthesis: the entry signal is NOT meaningfully better than regime-matched random timing where it matters. (1) Event level: at every actual entry the rule buys a small, real burst of continuation - +4h cost-adjusted excess of +0.22 to +0.40 ATR on all four symbols (90th-98th percentile vs 1000 regime-matched in-session control portfolios; sign robust to median, alternative fill, and no-cost recomputation) - but the information decays within a day and, on FX, inverts: EURUSD -0.57 ATR excess by +72h (adds -1.96), USDJPY -0.93 ATR by +24h (1.7th percentile) because the breakout rule selects into catastrophic yen reversals (11/96 entries within 24h of >5 ATR adverse moves). (2) Engine level, with a seeded random signal matched to the real signal's per-regime fire rate and side mix and charged identical spread/commission/swap under identical gates and exits (200 seeds/symbol): EURUSD +1.06% = 91.0th percentile (above-average draw, not significant), GBPUSD -1.23% = 84.5th (better-than-random timing that still loses), USDJPY -4.21% = 44.0th (pure noise), XAUUSD +1.73% = 29.5th (WORSE than random - 84.5% of random-entry runs on gold are positive, mean +3.94%). XAUUSD is the decisive case: it is the only symbol with genuine multi-day selection skill at the signal level (+2.07 ATR excess at 72h, 99.9th percentile), yet the system converts that into less money than random timing, because the scale-out/trail exit stack books 70% of the position by 2.2R and cannot monetize the drift the entries select. Answer to the dimension question: the entry rule contributes at most a marginal, short-horizon timing effect worth roughly +2-3 return points over random on EURUSD/GBPUSD (inside the noise envelope), zero on USDJPY, and negative net contribution on XAUUSD; the EA's headline positives are an unremarkable draw (EURUSD) and gold regime drift (XAUUSD), not entry skill. Canonical measured runs were first reproduced trade-for-trade identical before any counterfactual.
analysis.caveats: All results inherit the screening engine's fill model: H1 bars aggregated from M15, constant fallback spreads (10/15/28/16 points; no real spread series), $2.5/side/lot commission, approximate swap points - signal quality on real tick fills could differ. Horizons are measured in H1 trading bars (weekend gaps compressed), identically for events and controls. Event-study samples are small (96-158 units/symbol) and units within a trend episode are correlated (pyramid adds share regimes), so control-portfolio percentiles overstate independence; per-event bootstrap CIs are the honest check and they fail to separate from controls on EURUSD at all horizons and on most FX horizons. The engine-level random signal matches raw per-bar per-regime fire frequency, not the clustering of real fires, so random runs traded ~20-35% fewer units; the per-tranche expectancy percentiles (which normalize for this) agree directionally with the return percentiles. USDJPY's random distribution includes 31/200 runs that breach official FTMO rules; excluding them would shift the real strategy's percentile somewhat lower (survivor runs average better returns). Percentile ranks use mid-rank convention. Seeds fixed (event study BASE_SEED 20260714, 1000 seeds/horizon; engine BASE_SEED 11-14M by symbol, 200 seeds; robustness 987654321, 2000 bootstrap draws).

verdict.reasoning: VERIFICATION METHOD (all independent re-implementations, fresh seed streams unrelated to the analyst's, identical costs charged to controls, no look-ahead; scripts saved for reproducibility): (1) verify_random_entry_engine.py first reproduced all four canonical measured runs trade-for-trade identical against the on-disk engine (returns exact to 1e-9; ledgers identical at 172/171/142/253 tranches), confirming the comparison baseline. It then re-ran the engine-level random-entry test with fresh sha256-derived seeds, 200/symbol, in two variants: (A) the analyst's design (unconditional per-regime fire rate) and (B) a fairness probe with the fire rate conditioned on in-session bars, because run_backtest only consults signal() in-session and verify_firerates.py showed the real signal fires ~2x its unconditional rate in-session (e.g. GBPUSD 0.0494 vs 0.0246 long) — the analyst's control therefore under-fired at the actual decision points, which is exactly why their random runs traded only 66-68 units vs the real 100-105 on EUR/GBP. (2) verify_event_study.py re-derived the event-study numbers from scratch. (3) verify_gbp_matched_count.py re-derived the one surprising result a second way with the trade-count confound removed entirely (fire probability calibrated so random converts ~the real unit count). RESULTS — CONFIRMED: Variant A percentiles all reproduce within Monte-Carlo error (EURUSD 88.0 vs claimed 91.0; GBPUSD 88.5 vs 84.5; USDJPY 46.0 vs 44.0; XAUUSD 33.0 vs 29.5; binomial se ±2.0-3.5 at 200 seeds); XAUUSD random median +3.64% vs claimed +3.60% with real +1.73% below it and 158/200 random runs positive (claimed 169/200) — the decisive gold claim (regime drift that random timing harvests better) is confirmed and STRENGTHENS under variant B (random mean +5.45%, real at 25th pctile); EURUSD stays below the 95th under every control variant (88.0/90.0, and count-matching would push it lower since variant B over-trades 118 vs 100 units); USDJPY is noise everywhere (46.0/62.0); event-study numbers reproduce almost exactly (EURUSD +4h excess +0.348 ATR at 94.5th vs claimed +0.354/94.8; EURUSD +72h inversion -0.550/22.1st vs -0.565/21.8; GBPUSD +4h +0.407/97.6th; USDJPY +4h +0.221/88.4th; XAUUSD +4h +0.285/96.5th; XAUUSD +72h +2.067/~100th vs claimed +2.069/99.9); real-signal fire-rate stats exact (194/8645 bull, 192/8644 bear on EURUSD, etc.). REFUTED — the headline's universal claim "adds no system-level expectancy over regime-matched random timing on ANY symbol — none clears 95" fails on GBPUSD once the control is fairly calibrated: with in-session-conditioned fire rates (113 units vs real 105) the real -1.23% sits at the 99.0th percentile (0/200 random runs positive, random mean -6.30%), and in the second, count-matched derivation (108 units vs real 105, removing all cost-drag confound) it sits at the 97.5th percentile of returns and 98.5th of expectancy (1/200 random runs positive, random mean -6.26%, sd 1.94). Per-unit, real GBP entries lose ~-0.012%/unit vs ~-0.058 to -0.062%/unit for random at any frequency — a ~5x timing advantage worth roughly +5 return points that the analyst's own per-tranche normalization (92.5th) and event study (+4h CI separating) already hinted at but the headline dismissed. The headline's "84.5th" is not a wrong number under their method; the method's control under-fires by ~35%, and the correct conclusion for GBPUSD flips from "no expectancy added" to "significant timing skill destroyed by venue costs/exits." Secondary overreach: "short-lived (+4h)" contradicts the analyst's own (and my verified) XAUUSD result — selection skill there persists and grows to +72h (+2.07 ATR, ~100th pctile); it is short-lived on FX only. The program-level bottom line (no deployable edge; EURUSD positive an unremarkable draw; XAUUSD positive regime drift the exit stack converts worse than random; challenge-funding unjustified) SURVIVES — but the WHY-dimension answer must be corrected per symbol. Caveats: percentile MC error ±2-3.5 points at 200 seeds; all results inherit the screening engine's H1/constant-spread fill model; variant B slightly over-trades on EURUSD (118 vs 100 units) so its EURUSD percentile (90.0) is an upper bound — EURUSD remains not significant either way.
verdict.corrected_headline: Entry-vs-random is symbol-split, not uniformly null: EURUSD +1.06% sits at only the ~88-91st percentile of 200 regime-matched random-entry engine runs (not significant), USDJPY -4.21% at the ~44-62nd (pure noise), and XAUUSD +1.73% at the ~25-33rd — significantly WORSE than random (random mean +3.9 to +5.5%, median +3.6%), confirming the gold profit is regime drift the exit stack converts worse than random timing does; but on GBPUSD the prior control under-fired ~35% at the engine's actual in-session decision points, and with the fire rate session-conditioned and unit count matched (108 vs 105) the real -1.23% sits at the 97.5-99th percentile (random mean ~-6.3%, ≤1/200 runs positive) — GBPUSD entry timing IS significantly better than random and the symbol loses on venue costs/exits instead. The +4h timing burst (+0.22 to +0.41 ATR, 88-98th pctile) is real on all four symbols and short-lived on FX, but on XAUUSD selection skill persists to +72h (+2.07 ATR, ~100th pctile) and is still not monetized. Bottom line unchanged — no deployable entry edge anywhere — but the WHY differs per symbol: no timing skill (EURUSD/USDJPY), timing skill destroyed by costs/exits (GBPUSD), and multi-day selection skill un-monetized while underperforming its own regime drift (XAUUSD).

analysis.headline: The confluence filters do not earn their keep: no rung of the attribution ladder has a statistically credible OOS edge on any symbol (best t=1.39, never >=2), the vol-regime filter binds on only 2 of 2,141 raw candidates (rung4==rung3 to the cent on 3 of 4 symbols), and on the development symbol EURUSD the filters add +$12,533 in-sample vs only +$1,182 out-of-sample (10.6:1) — the signature of in-sample tuning dressed over a raw breakout whose expectancy is negative everywhere in-sample (unit PF 0.67-0.95).

analysis.conclusion: The confluence stack is selection dressing over a structurally losing signal, with one partial exception. Verdict by filter: (1) the vol-regime guard (ATR ratio<=2.5) is a filter in name only — it vetoes 0.14% of all raw candidates and produces bit-identical results on 3 of 4 symbols; (2) the candle body/wick confirmation is noise-level — it removes 6-8% of candidates with sub-$10/unit, sign-inconsistent expectancy effects; (3) the entry buffer and HTF H4+D1 stacks do all the sample reduction (~4x fewer units, ~80% of raw candidates vetoed) and do genuinely raise per-unit expectancy on EURUSD (OOS mean $9 -> $81/unit), but the evidence never strengthens (t plateaus at 1.36 while n collapses 116->28), the same filters flip signs on other symbols (buffer destroys gold's only OOS-positive cell; HTF craters USDJPY in-sample), and on the development symbol every filter helps IS ~10x more than OOS with in-sample expectancy still negative after all of them. Answering the dimension question 'why no edge': the raw 20-bar Donchian+EMA breakout has negative per-trade expectancy on all four symbols in-sample (unit PF 0.67-0.95 before filters), so the filters had nothing to purify — they were tuned to minimize EURUSD's historical losses, which mechanically loads their benefit in-sample, shrinks the OOS sample to sizes (22-46 units) where PF 1.2-1.87 is indistinguishable from luck, and under FTMO guards their main measurable function is keeping a losing strategy from freezing the account at the 8% soft floor. No rung, on any symbol, guarded or unguarded, produces an OOS edge that survives a basic t-test; pooled across symbols the OOS expectancy is within +/-0.03R of zero at every rung.
analysis.caveats: 1) Rung 0 as specified retains the H1 EMA50/200 stack + rising-EMA condition (inseparable from signal() by config) — this ladder attributes the five confluence filters, not the EMA trend gate; the direction-residue check confirmed the candle degenerate case never binds, so rung 0 is otherwise a true raw breakout. 2) Trade sets across rungs are not strictly nested (position occupancy, daily caps, and the latched profit lock make entries path-dependent), so per-rung deltas are net portfolio effects, not per-signal marginals; the position-independent census was run precisely to cross-check this and agrees. 3) Unit-level t-stats treat units as independent, but pyramid adds within one trend are correlated, so the reported t-values are, if anything, OVERSTATED — which only strengthens the no-edge conclusion. 4) Everything inherits the screening engine's H1 OHLC pessimistic-fill model, fallback (constant) spreads, and approximate swap; none of these caveats can rescue a filter whose veto count is zero. 5) IS/OOS unit assignment follows the ledger's oos flag (entry-bar side of the 70/30 split). 6) All runs deterministic — no randomness, so no seeds were required.

analysis.headline: The exit engine is a confirmed negative-alpha component at scale: on identical entries, identical spread and commission, its realized exits sit at or below the 1st percentile of 400 signal-free random-exit portfolios on all four symbols, giving back +74.8R total across 459 units (EURUSD +11.3R, GBPUSD +13.9R, USDJPY +27.4R, XAUUSD +22.3R), with the leak living almost entirely in the hold-to-stop path (-118.2R on the 294 stop-terminated units) and the break-even-at-TP1 stop move being the only mechanism whose removal helps consistently (+25.0R full-sample, +4.1R OOS, +6.9pp return across the four symbols).

analysis.conclusion: ANSWER TO THE DIMENSION - the exit engine leaks, a lot, on every symbol, and the prior 16R M5 finding was not a gold quirk. Holding entries, path, spread and commission fixed, the EA's exit machinery realizes 0th-1st-percentile outcomes versus signal-free random exits in the same holding windows: +74.8R total give-back across 459 units (~0.16R per unit), positive in-sample AND out-of-sample on all four symbols. Decomposition: (1) THE LEAK IS THE HOLD-TO-STOP PATH, not the scale-outs - the 294 units that terminate at a stop give back -118.2R vs random while winner-terminated units actually beat random by +43R; stops by construction execute at each window's adverse extreme, and the engine routes 64% of units there. (2) THE MOST CONSISTENTLY DESTRUCTIVE SINGLE MECHANISM IS BE-AT-TP1: patching out the stop-to-entry move (with break_even_r off, all else intact) is the only ablation that helps nearly everywhere (+25.0R full, +4.1R OOS, GBPUSD flips from -1.23% to +1.75%). It converts trades that just proved +1R of momentum into scratch-outs on normal retracement. (3) WEEKEND FLATTEN is the largest destroyer on XAUUSD only (+33R/+10.4pp if removed) - that is truncated long-gold beta, and it SAVES money on USDJPY, so it is not a generic defect. (4) EARLY SCALE-OUT is a wash (saves FX chop, cuts gold trend; negative OOS when removed) and (5) PYRAMIDING contributes nothing (+3.8R full, -1.5R OOS, sign-unstable). Strategic implication for 'why no edge': fixing the exits cannot rescue the EA - the ~+73R recoverable by matching random-exit timing would only lift the system from slightly negative to roughly what an unconditional exit gets, the FX entries decay to negative expectancy by 72-120 bars (USDJPY is negative at every horizon - an entry problem, not an exit problem), and the spectacular let-run numbers on gold (+256R, +20.5% engine return) are reproducible long-beta, not strategy alpha. The exit engine destroys expectancy the entries never had.
analysis.caveats: 1) Counterfactual exits use H1 bar closes while actual stop tranches fill intra-bar at the stop price under the engine's deliberately pessimistic model (stop-before-target, gap fills at worse-of); real stops do fill at stop prices so this is realistic-to-conservative, but a small part of the measured leak is fill-model asymmetry rather than pure timing. 2) Random-exit windows are bounded by the ACTUAL exit time, so the benchmark inherits the engine's loss-bounding; it answers 'was the timing inside the window any good', not 'what should the policy be'. 3) Per-unit counterfactuals hold entries fixed and ignore portfolio feedback (a unit held longer would block subsequent entries via max_units and daily caps); the full-engine ablation ladder captures those interactions and agrees directionally everywhere. 4) Fixed-horizon and let-run policies hold over weekends and carry no stop (horizons) - FTMO standard (non-Swing) accounts prohibit weekend holds, so the XAU weekend give-back is only recoverable on a Swing-type account. 5) Swap points in the broker meta are approximate mid-2025 snapshots; swap adjustments (reported separately, commission cancels exactly) trim but never overturn any conclusion. 6) 24h/72h/120h horizons are counts of H1 bars (trading hours), not calendar hours. 7) The BE-at-TP1 ablation required patching one hardcoded engine line (unit.stop = unit.entry after TP1); the patch is a single-line replacement asserted unique in source. 8) All numbers are from the corrected screening engine on ~2.8y of real Deriv M15 aggregated to H1 - this quantifies WHERE the canonical results lose expectancy; it validates no live edge for any variant (the +20.5% XAU stop-flip-only-no-weekend run is unvalidated beta riding, DSR-ungated, and breaches no FTMO guard only in this one sample).

analysis.conclusion: ANSWER (a) — is GROSS positive, IS and OOS? Only EURUSD has positive gross in both derivations (+0.057R/unit rerun, +0.094R same-path), but it is 100% concentrated in the 28-unit OOS window: IS gross is −$651/+$102 (≈0) depending on derivation. GBPUSD gross ≈ 0 with unstable sign (−$1,093 rerun vs +$939 same-path; IS ≈ −$139, OOS +$1,078). USDJPY gross is decisively NEGATIVE both ways, IS and OOS (−0.199R rerun, −0.094R same-path; IS −$2,383, OOS −$433). XAUUSD frictionless gross ≈ 0 (−$51); its canonical-path gross is IS-only (+$3,871 IS, −$670 OOS) and its positive net at 16-pt spread is demonstrably path luck (net is NEGATIVE at 0-8 pt spreads). ANSWER (b) — what do costs consume and which dominates? EURUSD: costs $1,901 = 64% of same-path gross; spread dominates (59% of costs; 0.035R/unit), then commission (29%), swap (12%). GBPUSD: costs $2,172 = 231% of a $939 gross; spread dominates (67%). USDJPY: gross already negative before costs; spread is the biggest cost (0.069R/unit — yes, the 28-pt spread bites hardest here) but swap is actually a +$1,275 CREDIT (long-JPY carry), and zeroing ALL costs still loses 6.1%. XAUUSD: costs $1,471 = 46% of (IS-only) gross; SWAP dominates (53% — the −45/night long-gold financing, 0.0155R/unit), spread only 36%, commission 11%. Commission is a minor cost everywhere (0.003-0.020R/unit). ANSWER (c) — break-even spread and plausibility: EURUSD ~19.5-20 pts (two methods agree) vs 10 modeled — plausibly available on FTMO (effective ~2-10 pts), so EURUSD is the only symbol where the venue is NOT the binding constraint; GBPUSD needs 2.4 pts (0.24 pips) — not available anywhere; USDJPY needs −29 pts (you'd have to be PAID the spread) — impossible; XAUUSD's nominal 68 pts is meaningless because the response surface is non-monotone noise around a ≈0 gross. VERDICT: this is the unfixable kind. Three of four symbols (GBPUSD, USDJPY, XAUUSD) have gross expectancy that is zero or negative BEFORE any costs — no cost engineering (tighter spread, lower commission, swap-free account) can create an edge that isn't there, and USDJPY's signal is outright wrong on this data. EURUSD alone shows real-looking gross that survives realistic FTMO costs, but its in-sample gross is zero and the entire edge is one 28-unit OOS window — consistent with the program's standing conclusion that this is not a validated edge. The EA's problem is the signal, not the venue.
analysis.caveats: 1) The engine is a conservative H1 OHLC screening model (intrabar ambiguity resolved against the strategy), not MT5 tick parity — absolute nets are pessimistic but the gross-vs-cost structure should hold. 2) Re-run ladder deltas mix true cost with path divergence (trade sets change 3-16% between rungs and cascade through daily caps/profit locks/pyramids); the same-path decomposition on canonical fills is the authoritative attribution and reconciles to the cent, but its spread term is the first-order crossing bill (spread × lots) — spread's second-order effect (shifted hit probabilities of TPs/stops) is only visible in the re-runs, where it is inside the noise band. 3) Net-vs-spread is non-monotone (±$1,000-3,000 path noise), so break-even spreads are trend crossings, not sharp thresholds; the two independent derivations agree for EURUSD (19.5 vs 20.1 pts) which is the only symbol where the number matters. 4) Swap points are the meta file's APPROXIMATE mid-2025 FTMO-style values and USDJPY's tick value is a point-in-time USD conversion; real financing varies daily — the XAUUSD swap-dominance and USDJPY swap-credit findings are directionally robust but not exact. 5) FTMO live-feed spread figures cited for plausibility are typical published/observed values, not measured on FTMO's feed this session (the repo's ftmo/spread-check exists for that). 6) Single 70/30 chronological split; OOS buckets are small (22-46 units) and no significance testing was done here — the OOS-positive FX gross readings are well within small-sample luck, per the parity-audit precedent. 7) All runs FTMO-guarded (canonical protocol); guard interactions are part of the measured path by design. 8) No randomness anywhere (deterministic engine and script), so no seeding was required despite the harness rule.

analysis.conclusion: The EA's positive residue (EURUSD +1.06%, XAUUSD +1.73%) is regime luck riding directional sub-windows, and the EA is strictly worse than trivial trend beta. (1) Side decomposition: EURUSD profit is 100%+ short-sided against a rising full-sample drift, concentrated in exactly two EUR-down windows (autumn 2023 +$1,949; H1 2026 +$1,899 — the latter is 83% of the celebrated OOS PF 1.84, from just 5 units), with 2024 bleeding −$2,114 in between; XAUUSD longs (145 units) net PF 1.04 ≈ zero through a +107% gold bull, and the EA LOST money in 2025 (gold +65%) and OOS (gold +18%). (2) Baselines under identical costs/sizing: the EA beats the two-line baseline only on EURUSD (where all baselines lose and the EA's own profit is noise); on GBPUSD/USDJPY/XAUUSD it underperforms a no-thought EMA50/200 long/flat follower by $5.7k/$16.3k/$28.9k respectively, and USDJPY B&H with carry beats it by ~$36k. (3) Concentration/bootstrap: top-3 units carry 170% (EURUSD) and 118% (XAUUSD) of full-period net; 10,000-resample bootstraps put every symbol's net inside the zero band (p(net≤0) = 0.33–0.93). (4) Time stability: no symbol makes money across regimes — each profitable cell of the yearly table coincides with one directional window whose sign the EA happened to be positioned for, and adjacent regimes take it back. Verdict for the parent question: the EA adds nothing beyond (badly harvested) beta — its filter/guard stack suppresses trend capture and losses alike, leaving cost-laden noise whose occasional positive residue is a handful of lucky units in trending sub-windows. The apparent EURUSD "edge" (+1.06%, OOS PF 1.84) is the single strongest piece of regime-luck evidence, not the exception to it.
analysis.caveats: (a) Bootstrap treats units as iid; pyramid adds are correlated within a move (e.g. XAUUSD's #2/#3 top units are 2023-09-25 15:00 and 2023-09-26 13:00 shorts in the same swing), so true concentration is worse and p-values optimistic — this biases AGAINST my conclusion's strength, not for it. (b) Baselines hold overnight and over weekends (the EA flattens Fridays and is session-gated), so they carry gap risk the EA avoids and slightly undercharged weekend swap (engine convention: one charge per calendar-date change); their max drawdowns are 6–31% vs the EA's 4–5%, so raw-net comparisons flatter the baselines — the DD-normalized comparison (still ~9x in the baseline's favor on XAUUSD) is the fair one. (d) All numbers come from the conservative H1-OHLC screening engine (stop-before-target), not tick parity. (e) Baselines size one 0.35% position vs the EA's up to 3 concurrent 0.35% units, so the baselines use LESS peak risk. (f) GBPUSD uses the relaxedgate ledger per the task; the plain GBPUSD.json (−1.01%) does not change any conclusion. (g) Buy-and-hold windows start at bar 210 (engine warmup) for symmetry with the EA's first possible entry.

analysis.headline: The EA's edge is statistically indistinguishable from zero and its best-looking number is pure selection: pooled expectancy across all 4 symbols is NEGATIVE (-0.017R/unit, cluster t=-0.27, n=459), the single best cell in the whole results grid (EURUSD OOS, +0.259R, day-clustered t=1.26, p=0.22) is below the expected maximum of just 8 pure-noise t-stats (1.46) and less than half the Bonferroni hurdle implied by the >=9 documented design decisions (z>=2.77), the celebrated IS-negative/OOS-positive "paradox" is reproduced by 7.4-10.7% of random re-splits of the same trades (and the mirror-image flip occurs on XAUUSD), and the sample is 30-50x too small to detect a +0.05R edge (need ~3,022-5,003 units vs 100-459 available, i.e. 19-137 years of trading).

The observed best t (1.26) is BELOW the expected maximum of even 8 pure-noise trials (1.46) and ~45% of the N=9 Bonferroni hurdle: the grid underperforms what noise-plus-selection alone would be expected to produce.

metrics.value: p(random 70/30 re-split OOS mean >= +0.2587) = 0.074 unit-permutation (10,000 perms, seed 7; range 0.061-0.094 over 100 seeds) and 0.107 week-block permutation (52 blocks; range 0.078-0.133); joint pattern (IS <= -0.052 AND OOS >= +0.259) = same 0.074/0.107; ANY IS<0<OOS sign flip occurs in 28.0%/31.0% of random splits

Verdict: the IS-negative/OOS-positive pattern is variance, not a late-emerging edge - and since IS drove the 9-step design selection, OOS was the only untouched split and it is insignificant.

metrics.name: Sample adequacy for a +0.05R true edge
metrics.value: sd(R)=0.981 (EURUSD) / 0.990 (pooled) -> n = 3,022 (5% two-sided, 80% power) / 5,003 (95% power) per EURUSD sd; pooled sd gives 3,075/5,092. metrics.definition: One-sample z-approximation n = ((z_0.975 + z_power) * sd / 0.05)^2. The screen can only resolve per-unit edges ~5x larger than the +0.05R that would plausibly matter; it is structurally incapable of validating (or refuting) an edge of realistic size at this sample.

analysis.conclusion: STATISTICAL VERDICT: there is no statistically detectable edge, and the reported positives are selection artifacts on an inadequate sample. (1) Honest per-unit expectancy is +0.035R on EURUSD (t=0.31 after day-clustering) and NEGATIVE pooled across the 4 screened symbols (-0.017R, t=-0.27, weekly-block bootstrap CI [-0.160,+0.108]); every per-symbol CI comfortably straddles zero and the strongest statistic in the entire grid is USDJPY's negative t=-1.23. (2) The one number that looks alive - EURUSD OOS +0.259R - carries a clustered t of 1.26 (p=0.22), which fails even a nominal unadjusted 5% test, sits BELOW the expected maximum of 8 pure-noise t-stats (1.46) generated by simply picking the best of 4 symbols x 2 splits, and is less than half the z>=2.77-3.48 that surviving the >=9 documented sequential design decisions (times 4 symbols, times 3 re-screens) would require. (3) The IS-negative/OOS-positive 'paradox' is not evidence of a real edge that emerged late: 7.4-10.7% of seeded random re-splits of the same trade sequence produce an equally good OOS, the qualitative sign flip is a 28-31% base-rate event, and XAUUSD exhibits the mirror-image flip in the same results set - exactly the two-sided scatter variance produces. (4) Even if a true +0.05R edge existed, this harness could not see it: at sd(R)=0.98 per unit you need ~3,000-5,000 units and there are 100 (EURUSD) to 459 (pooled) - i.e. 19-137 years of trading at the observed signal frequency. The +1.06% EURUSD headline is therefore an unrejected null dressed as a marginal positive: the honest statement is that after ~dozens of implicit trials the best remaining split is weaker than noise-plus-selection alone would predict. Reproducible scripts and JSON outputs are in backtest/audit/ (stats_honesty_01/02).
analysis.caveats: Unit R uses risk budgets recovered exactly from the ledger (pnl/r per tranche) - verified to reconcile with net_profit to the cent and against reason-weight reconstruction (0/100 mismatches), but inherits the canonical run's assumptions (fallback spreads, approximate swap snapshot, H1 stop-first fills). Entry-day clustering may still understate multi-day regime dependence; the weekly-block bootstrap addresses one level up but true regime blocks could be longer, which would make the t-stats even weaker, not stronger. The permutation null assumes exchangeability of unit R over time, which ignores genuine regime drift - but a clustered t of 1.26 cannot be rescued by any regime story, and the drift argument cuts against the OOS reading too (nothing guarantees the OOS regime persists). The 9-trial multiplicity floor counts only DOCUMENTED accepted decisions; rejected parameter values during development were not logged, so every hurdle quoted is a lower bound. Power numbers use the z-approximation (exact t-based n is ~1-2 units higher). GBPUSD uses the relaxedgate ledger per the canonical results table; the stricter GBPUSD.json variant is itself one more unlogged trial. Bootstrap/permutation p-values are seeded (seeds 7/42) with 100-seed stability ranges reported; all randomness is reproducible from the saved scripts.

analysis.conclusion: VERDICT ON THE DIMENSION: the underlying premise is dead where the EA needs it and redundant where it isn't. (1) On EURUSD and GBPUSD, raw H1 Donchian-breakout continuation is statistically indistinguishable from zero at every horizon from 1 to 48 bars (all bootstrap CIs straddle zero, best permutation p=0.085), and the point estimates (~0.09-0.17 ATR at the best horizon) are about the size of ONE round-trip cost - there is no pre-cost drift for any machinery to harvest. (2) On USDJPY the premise was genuinely alive in 2023-24 (h12 +0.74 then +0.29 ATR, full-sample perm p=0.011) but decayed monotonically and inverted to significantly NEGATIVE (-0.37 ATR, CI excludes zero) in 2026 - the EA is trading a dead regime, which is exactly why its ledger shows -4.21%. analysis.caveats: Sample is ~2.8-3 years (Sep 2023 - Jul 2026) on a single venue (Deriv M15 aggregated to complete-H1 bars); 2023 and 2026 are partial years, so by-year cells have unequal n (202-742 events). Breakout events overlap heavily inside trends - the calendar-month block bootstrap (1000 resamples, seeded) absorbs within-month serial correlation but effective sample size is far below the nominal 1839-2006 events, so moderate effects (GBPUSD h24 +0.17) can hide in the wide CIs; absence of significance is not proof of exactly zero, but any drift below ~one round-trip cost is untradeable regardless. Permutation p-values are per-symbol/per-horizon (20 tests) without multiplicity correction; USDJPY's full-sample p=0.003-0.011 would weaken under correction (its 2026 inversion is the more decision-relevant fact). Continuation is close-to-close and spread-free by design; the EA's realized PnL passes this drift through a 2.5-ATR stop, scale-outs, and session filters, so positive mean drift is necessary but not sufficient for EA profit - the converse (no drift implies no edge) is the load-bearing direction here. Cost yardstick uses the canonical fallback spreads and a point-in-time USDJPY tick value, not historical spread series. The drift adjustment subtracts full-sample unconditional drift scaled by the events' long/short mix (recomputed inside each bootstrap resample); it removes static drift, not time-varying regime effects - on XAUUSD some 'adjusted' continuation may still be bull-regime clustering rather than breakout information. signal() was tested with H1 EMA50/200 and ATR exactly as the engine computes them, but without the session window, HTF confluence, or vol-regime gates (the A_session_only variant shows session filtering alone changes little); the D subset was assert-verified to nest inside the buffer+candle subset.
